verses.text: Praise the LORD! Thank the LORD because he’s good. His faithful love lasts forever.
Who could tell everything the LORD has done in his power? Who could give him all the praise he deserves?
Blessed are those who stand up for justice and do what’s right every time.
Remember me, LORD, when you show favor to your people. Come save me too,
so I can see the people you chose thrive, share your nation’s joy, and celebrate with those who belong to you.
We’ve sinned just like our ancestors. We’ve done wrong. We’ve acted wickedly.
Our ancestors missed what your wonders in Egypt meant. They forgot how often you’d shown them faithful love. They rebelled right there at the Red Sea.
Even so, he saved them for the sake of his name, to show just how strong he is.
He rebuked the Red Sea, and it dried up. He led them through the depths as if they were walking through a desert.
He saved them from the grip of those who hated them and bought them back from the enemy’s hand.
The waters covered their enemies. Nobody was left.
Then they believed his words and sang his praise.
But they forgot what he’d done almost immediately. They didn’t wait for his advice.
They let their cravings take over in the desert and put God to the test in the wasteland.
He gave them what they asked for, but left them wasting away inside.
In the camp they grew jealous of Moses and of Aaron, the LORD’s holy one.
The ground opened and swallowed Dathan and buried Abiram’s group.
A fire broke out among them and burned up the wicked.
At Horeb they made a calf and bowed down to a statue cast from metal.
They traded their glory for a statue of a bull that eats grass.
They forgot God, the one who’d saved them and done great things in Egypt,
wonders in the land of Ham and things that filled people with awe at the Red Sea.
He said he would destroy them, but Moses, the one he chose, stepped into the breach before him and turned his wrath away so he wouldn’t wipe them out.
Then they turned up their noses at the good land and refused to believe his word.
They grumbled in their tents and ignored the LORD’s voice.
So he swore that he’d bring them down in the wilderness,
bring down their descendants among the nations, and scatter them across other lands.
They joined themselves to Baal Peor and ate sacrifices offered to the dead.
What they did made God angry, and a plague broke out among them.
Then Phinehas stood up and carried out judgment, and the plague stopped.
That was counted to him as righteousness for every generation to come.
They also made God angry at the waters of Meribah, and Moses suffered because of them.
They rebelled against his spirit, and Moses spoke without thinking.
They didn’t destroy the peoples as the LORD had commanded.
Instead they mixed with the nations and picked up their ways.
They served their idols, and those idols became a trap for them.
They even sacrificed their sons and daughters to demons.
They spilled innocent blood, the blood of their own sons and daughters, offering them to the idols of Canaan. Blood polluted the land.
Their own deeds made them unclean. By what they did, they sold themselves out like prostitutes.
So the LORD’s anger burned against his people. He came to despise his own inheritance.
He handed them over to the nations. People who hated them took charge of them.
Their enemies oppressed them and forced them to live under their power.
He rescued them over and over, but they kept making plans to rebel and ended up brought low by their own wrongdoing.
Still, when he heard them cry out, he paid attention to their suffering.
He remembered his covenant with them and relented because his faithful love was so great.
He made the people who took them captive feel compassion for them.
Save us, LORD our God! Gather us back from the nations so we can thank your holy name and celebrate as we praise you!
Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from forever to forever! Let everyone say, “Amen.” Praise the LORD!
